description:
FILED s510 (Fable, 2026-10-06) from the perf round 40 review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s510/review/p40/w1.pl .. w8.pl); main 9364ae68 and the s510p tree alike.

  use warnings; no warnings "uninitialized";
  print join(", ", 1, undef, "x"), "\n";          perl: `1, , x` and NOTHING on stderr
                                                  PCL : stderr `Use of uninitialized value in join or string` (no "at FILE line N"), then `1, , x`

DISCRIMINATED: `join(",", @a)` with an undef ELEMENT is silent (w4, w7); `"a" . $u` and `"b$u"` are silent (w8); only the call whose arguments are all LITERALS warns, the message is perl\x27s own wording without a location, and it comes BEFORE the program\x27s first output -- so it is written by the transpiler process while it folds the constant call under its own `use warnings`, not by the program.  Consequences: (1) the program\x27s `no warnings` cannot switch it off; (2) with warnings ON the text lacks perl\x27s " at FILE line N."; (3) it appears on the run that transpiles and never again from the cache -- a first-run-only difference on stderr (the #2702 family of symptoms, different cause).

NOT MEASURED (the cheap next step): which folds can warn -- grep the constant-folding site(s) in Pl/ (where a builtin call with literal operands is evaluated in the compiler) and try `lc(undef)`, `"a" . undef`, `undef + 1`, `sprintf("%s", undef)`, `substr("abc", 5)`, `1 / 0` (a DIE in the compiler?), `"abc" + 1` ("isn\x27t numeric").  A fold that can warn or die in the compiler must either not fold that operand shape or fold under `no warnings` + emit the run-time form so the PROGRAM\x27s warning state decides.
subject: LOUD, small (pre-existing): the COMPILER\x27s own perl warning reaches the user\x27s stderr -- `join(", ", 1, undef, "x")` with a LITERAL undef prints "Use of uninitialized value in join or string" at transpile time, also under `no warnings "uninitialized"`, and only on the run that transpiles
